idle: An object stands upright and breathes quietly with relaxed arms.
walk: An object walks forward at an easy pace with short heel-to-toe steps.
jog: An object jogs forward at a comfortable pace.
run: An object runs straight forward with quick alternating strides and bent elbows.
sprint: An object sprints straight forward at maximum speed with powerful arm drive and high knees.
sprint-race: An object races forward with long rapid strides and leans forward.
squat: An object bends both knees and lowers into a deep squat, then holds the squat.
prone: An object kneels, puts both hands down, then lies flat on its belly.
rise: An object pushes up from lying on its belly and stands upright.
jump: An object bends its knees, jumps once, then lands with both feet and bends its knees.
double-jump: An object makes a second jump in mid air, tucks both knees, then extends both feet to land.
wall-up: An object faces a vertical climbing wall and climbs upward with alternating hand reaches and foot steps.
wall-down: An object faces a vertical climbing wall and climbs down feet first using hands and feet.
wall-left: An object traverses sideways to its left on a climbing wall, reaching and stepping left.
wall-right: An object traverses sideways to its right on a climbing wall, reaching and stepping right.
mantle: An object hangs from a ledge, pulls both shoulders above its hands, places a knee on top and stands up on the platform.
stairs-up: An object walks upstairs one tread at a time, lifting alternate knees.
stairs-down: An object walks downstairs one tread at a time with controlled alternating steps.
tree: An object climbs a tree trunk, hugging it with both arms and stepping up with bent legs.
vault: An object vaults over a low barrier, plants one hand, swings both legs over and lands running.
ladder: An object climbs a vertical ladder alternating hands and feet.
turn-left: An object plants a foot while moving forward, pivots sharply to its left, then continues running.
turn-right: An object plants a foot while moving forward, pivots sharply to its right, then continues running.
race-dash: An object sprints forward quickly in a track race, rapidly pumping its arms and legs.
race-fast: An object runs as fast as possible in a straight line.
lower-face-down: An object kneels on the ground, leans forward onto both palms, extends both legs backward, and lies face down with chest against the ground.
prone-crawl: An object crawls forward on its stomach with its face down and elbows bent.
step-up: An object steps up a flight of stairs, lifting and placing one foot on each successive step.
step-down: An object steps down a flight of stairs one step at a time.
climb-onto-platform: An object climbs onto a platform by putting both hands on the edge, bringing a knee up and pushing itself into a standing position.
climb-pole: An object climbs a vertical pole hand over hand, pressing both feet against the pole.
vault-upright: An object runs toward a low hurdle, clears it with one leg leading and the torso upright, and lands on the leading foot.
vault-step: An object steps over a low fence and continues moving forward.
air-tuck: An object jumps straight up with both knees tucked, keeps its head above its feet, then extends both legs and lands.
wall-descend: An object climbs down a vertical ladder, looking at the ladder and lowering its feet one rung at a time.
kick-right: An object stands on its left leg and kicks a soccer ball forward with its right foot, then puts its right foot down.
kick-instep: An object takes a short step onto its left foot and swings the right leg forward to kick a ball along the ground.
wall-grip: An object climbs straight up a vertical wall with its chest upright, moving one hand and the opposite foot at a time.
jog-steady: An object jogs forward at a steady easy pace.
sprint-track: An object sprints forward on a flat running track.
sprint-fast: An object sprints forward as fast as it can.
sprint-strides: An object runs at full speed across a flat track, taking quick alternating strides.
sprint-race-pace: An object sprints straight ahead in a race, leaning forward and driving its arms.
sprint-long-strides: An object sprints at top speed on a flat track with long, rapid alternating strides.
sprint-straight: An object sprints very fast straight ahead, pumping its arms forcefully.
sprint-fast-strides: An object runs at full speed across a flat track, taking powerful, quick alternating strides and leaning forward.
sprint-race-straight: An object sprints down the straightaway of a 100-meter race at maximum speed.
idle-arms-low: An object stands upright and breathes quietly, with both arms hanging loosely at its sides, wrists beside the hips and gaze forward.
idle-at-ease: An object stands at rest with feet flat and still. Its hands rest naturally beside its thighs throughout a slight breathing motion.
jump-small-step: An object takes a short step, bends both knees and makes one small forward hop. Its elbows stay near its ribs and its hands stay at waist height as it lands softly on both feet.
jump-small-hop: An object makes one low two-footed jump from a shallow crouch and lands with soft knees. Arms swing gently at hip and waist height for balance.
jump-waist: An object jumps forward and lands on both feet. Its elbows are bent near its waist and its hands stay in front of its belly.
jump-over-line: An object jumps forward over a chalk line on the ground and lands with both feet. It keeps its bent arms low for balance.
jump-hands-forward: An object jumps forward from a crouch and lands on both feet. Both hands stay in front of the hips.
